lines.en: Another week as the world’s most sexually active teacher means another week to completely ruin the lives of everyone around me by simply showing up to class.
Oh. Sorry for the self-loathing so early in the morning. I just figured that if I got it all out of the way now, I’d be able to do whatever I want for the rest of the day without thinking at all.
Which, to be fair, is what I try to do most days to begin with.
However, I was notified of a very particular “holiday” through a phone call from my assistant this morning that has put me in a particularly passive aggressive mood.
Especially since it requires my full presence in the classroom at the risk of both Imani and me losing our jobs. And Imani has been kind enough to me so far that I don’t want to do that to her.
Also, I’m pretty sure she’s barely hanging on by a thread financially and she kind of needs this.
I slide open the door and prepare myself for the start of what I imagine will be the worst holiday ever- and that is saying a lot since things like Christmas exist.
But at least on Christmas you can come up with excuses to not pay attention to certain people.
: Good morning! Happy National Tsukasa Day!
: Tsukasa, how much did you pester our poor father to make this childish dream of yours a reality?
: It’s not a childish dream if I’m an ancient and powerful wizard. Just because there’s not National Touka Day doesn’t mean you can get mad at my holiday.
: Sensei is a very busy-
: Well...actually, that’s not true at all. Sensei is practically never busy.
: But he’s assuredly not going to start being busy when he’s preoccupied with silly games like this.
: Wrong again, dear sister. I’ve heard the games this adult plays and they are a lot louder than whatever is going on in this sorry excuse for a classroom.
: Why are you here?
: Because it’s National Tsukasa Day and I get to do whatever I want.
: So you chose to...come to high school?
: Yup!
: The train wasn’t very exciting, so I wanted to get a closer look at the true commoner mecca! A public school!
: I even had my personal tailor make an exact copy of my sister’s uniform so I can experience firsthand the pain she endures every day as she is turned into one of you!
: Sensei, how long is Tsukasa staying here?
: While I, too, would like to know the answer to that question, I’m more concerned about what sorts of games Tsukasa has heard you playing.
: To Ami, I have no idea what she’s talking about. And to Ayane, I assume she’ll only be here until the end of Tsukasa Day.
: Ahem! It is National Tsukasa Day! Don’t go leaving out words that describe how important it is.
: Also, National Tsukasa Day doesn’t end until next Wednesday because Father said so.
: Damn. I wish I was rich enough to change the way time works.
: You don’t have to be rich, Imani! All you have to do to change the way time works is get pregnant with Sensei’s baby. Well, at least according to Maya.
: What?
: I have absolutely no clue what she is talking about.
: With all due respect, Senpai, I think I’d rather take the money.
: You’re handsome and all, but if the way you treat my body is anything like the way you treat my mind, I can’t imagine that would be a very enjoyable experience.
: Luckily for you, I don’t intend on getting anyone preg-
: Stop paying attention to everyone not named Tsukasa on National Tsukasa Day!
: Right! Uhh...yeah.
: See, the issue with that is that I’m not exactly...good with kids that aren’t in high school yet. They make me feel weird. And even if today is National Tsukasa Day, you kind of...
: Well, you don’t belong here.
: Watch it, Imani. This girl may not look intimidating, but she holds our futures in the palms of her tiny hands.
: Are you two sure you are even teachers? Because I’m hearing a whole lot of slander and not so much teaching right now.
: And I suggest that if you two want to keep your jobs, that you...actually do them.
: I am so sorry that this is happening today. I tried my best to prevent it, but...alas.
: What can we even teach with someone your age here? You won’t be able to follow along.
: Do you take me for a lowly peasant? I have received only the highest forms of education from the most qualified teachers in all of Kumon-mi.
: Your meaningless squibbles disguised as educational lectures mean nothing before the greatness that is Tsukasa AKA “Tsurumi” Tsukioka of the Tsukioka family.
: Squibble? What’s a squibble?
: A word I made up that means “silly and pointless!” I call it a Tsukasology. Or a...Tsukasism. There’s another one right there.
: Creating new words is far detached from proper education, Tsukasa...AKA Tsurumi.
: Then try me! Ask me anything. I’m sure my answers will be far more acceptable than whatever these so-called “squobbles” would give you.
: But...no one calls them that.
What is the world’s oldest city?
: What is the world’s oldest city?
: Damascus, Syria!
: That's a highly contested topic as many people believe it to be Jericho. But Jericho was more like a large town than a city during its early years.
: Mother says Damascus isn’t all it’s cracked up to be, though. She visited there on one of her travels from before Kumon-mi was isolated.
: Did she get it right?
: I have no clue. I just asked a question thinking she wouldn’t know the answer.
: Never fear, Senpai. I will do my duties as your loyal peon and utilize the glory of my smart phone to- holy shit, she’s right.
: Of course she is...
How tall is Mt. Fuji?
: How tall is Mt. Fuji?
: Three-thousand, seven-hundred-seventy-six meters!
: I’m supposed to go there with Papa once we’re allowed to leave the city again.
: He says he’s going to buy part of the mountain so I can have my own little house there.
: Is that even legal?
: Everything is legal when you’re rich. But you wouldn’t know that since you’re not.
: That’s Ayane Amamiya you’re speaking to, Tsukasa. She comes from the second richest family in all of the city.
: Sorry. Can’t hear you from all the way up here in first place.
Who lives at the North Pole?
: If you’re so smart, how about you tell me who lives at the North Pole?
: Bruh.
: Sensei...
: The North Pole?
: Do you take me for a fool, commoner?
: Everyone knows that’s where Santa’s workshop is. That was barely even a question.
: Are you sure about that?
: Yes. Unless you mean to tell me it is my mother who has been returning my annual letters to him. And that would just be utter nonsense.
: Are you sure about that?
: Don’t do it, Sensei...
: Even you should draw the line at telling a little kid the truth about Santa Claus, Sensei. You’re better than this.
: The truth?
: Did something happen to Santa Claus?
: If he was evicted due to the waste produced by his workshop, I would not mind forgoing some of my allowance to assist him. He does tremendous work for this country and is an asset to all of us.
: Just drop it, Sensei. Before it’s too late.
: Fine. But I rest my case in showing that Tsukasa isn’t as smart as she thinks she is.
: Yes, but that is only because you asked her a question that all of those prestigious educators dared not ever speak about.
: Why is everybody acting so weird? All it takes is a little personal research to figure out the truth.
: Can you people not afford computers?
: What do you think, Senpai? It would feel kind of wrong getting rid of her now. But, like I said before, I’m not really the best when it comes to kids.
: And you think I am?
: Well, you became a teacher, didn’t you? You’ve gotta be at least a little good with them.
: Didn’t...you also become a teacher?
: Yeah, but I’ve still got time left.
: I’m only 31.
: Damn, that old already? Need me to go grab a cane from the nurse’s office?
: Again! You people refuse to pay attention to the one person you should be paying all of your attention to today!
: This insolence will not go unpunished! As soon as my father finds out about this, you two will never work another day in this town again! You-
: Tsukasa, please! They are doing their best! And all things considered, their best seems very good based on the standards of today’s public education system.
: Hah...This is exactly why the youth of the nation has become so lazy and unmotivated. No one gets the education they need anymore. Papa should really do something about that.
: I agree but, unfortunately, progress didn’t have much place to go after the creation of bubble wrap.
: Hey, Tsukasa. What are you doing here?
: Oh! The peasant girl from Mother’s onsen!
: And here I was thinking the strong scent of cheap perfume was just the way girls’ public schools smelled.
: Is it...really that strong? Because I’m trying something new and that wasn’t exactly the type of reaction I was looking for.
: What type of reaction were you looking for?
: A...positive one?
: Oh.
: Well, good luck.
: Th...That aside! How are things? How’s your mom?
: Things are great! As you may have noticed from all of the banners in the hall, today is National Tsukasa Day!
: Unfortunately, Mother had other matters to attend to, so she is unable to spend it with me. But that’s okay because my big sister and her teacher are looking after me.
: Which isn’t to say I wouldn’t be able to function on my own when I am much better and smarter than both of them. But laws will be laws.
: You do know what “laws” are, correct?
: Yes, Tsukasa. I do know what laws are.
: Good! I never know with you people.
: “You people” as in...commoners, right?
: Good job! Public education has not entirely failed you yet.
: That said, it would be wise to quit while you’re ahead and follow in the footsteps of your younger sister. She and I have big plans for this world.
: Yeah, you two have been talking a lot lately, haven’t you?
: Talking? We’re not just talking. We’re drafting business plans that are going to flip Kumon-mi on its head. People like us do not have time to simply “talk.”
: Well, would you maybe like to come over and discuss business in person sometime?
: Can your budget home fit more than two people inside of it?
: Uhh...yes.
: Just...probably not more than five.
: I can fit more people than that in my bathroom.
: Why is that...ever a thing you’d want to do?
: It’s not. But I can and I felt compelled to inform you of that.
: Either way, Chinami has been excited to see you again and I figure this would give you two a good chance to play together.
: I will consider it and consult with the rest of my business associates!
: If I do agree to play though, will you consider teaching Chinami and I the special game you played with your teacher at the onsen? Mother says it’s for adults, but I have proven today that I-
: MMMFMFMFMFMFMFFFFFMFHHFHFFF!!!!!
: Special game?...
: Onsen?...
: Hahaha! Kids, right?! Always making up stories!
: Oh, look. A stack of papers way at the...other end of the school that I need you to file.
: You trying to teach Chika how to time travel, Senpai?
: I have no idea what you’re talking about.
: And at an onsen? What does that mean for all of the other girls who had to stare at your drab-ass wallpaper while you were doin’ ‘em dirty?
: Is that really what you’re most concerned about?
: I’m an advocate for equality, Senpai. We all deserve onsens.
: Well, I’ll add you to the top of my...prospective onsen visit list now.
: Think saying that might be giving me a little too much attention on National Tsukasa Day, don’t you think?
: MMMFMFMFMFMFFHFHFHFFMMFMFM!!!!!!!! MMMMM!!!!!!!
: Tsukasa, what does Mother say about making a racket like that? Quiet down or you’ll attract negative press.
: MMMMMMMMMM!!!!!!!!!!!!
: Tsukasa...I’m gonna let you go now. But I kinda need you to not say anything about the onsen, okay? Nobody is supposed to know about that.
: MMMM! MMMMM! MMMM!!!
: Are you out of your mind?! Do you have any idea who I am?! Do you think it’s okay to just assault a princess?! I will have your head!
: But if you kill me, Chinami won’t want to do business with you anymore, so...your success kinda hinges on me in a way, doesn’t it?
: While it is true that an ally like her would certainly take us to the next level, I’m not quite sure if it is worth my own personal safety.
: What if I...promise not to grab your face anymore?
: That would be a start...but I am going to need something a little more than that.
: Uhh...
: You can eat...cereal when you come over to my place?
: C...Cereal? But Mother says cereal is a leading cause of diabetes and that there are much tastier and healthier alternatives.
: And while I’m sure she’s right...you do want a taste of commoner life, don’t you? What better taste than eating the same thing Chinami eats every morning inside of Chinami’s house?
: Think of it as a...research...project.
: You drive a hard bargain, peasant. That does sound like something that tickles my interest. However, I have one final adjustment I’d like to add to your offer.
: And that...adjustment is?
: Can my sister come too?
: What?
: It wouldn’t be fair if I got to experience something like that firsthand and she did not. I am simply doing this so that the two of us may remain on equal footing.
: It is the least I can do in exchange for intruding on her personal life by being here.
: Tsukasa...I don’t really need to-
: Sure, yeah. That’s actually...
: You know what? Why don’t we invite Sensei too?
: What?
: That seems unnecessary. Jeeves has no place in the same room as two serious and powerful businesswomen. And also Onee-chan.
: Why is Sensei...suddenly a part of this as well, Chika?
: Because I was looking for a good time to go do something lately and kind of need a babysitter since I have no idea how long it will take.
: Which isn’t to say I don’t trust you, Touka. I just...don’t really know if you'll be able to grasp any of the, uhh...commoner technology at my place.
: I mean...I guess I can come? I doubt I’ll be much help, though.
: Jeeves can wait in the lobby while the rest of us talk. That seems fair to me.
: I don’t believe Chika’s home is the type to have a lobby, Tsukasa. Sensei can wait in her rose garden instead.
: Sensei? You cool with that?
: Depends. Do you have a rose garden now?
: Who doesn’t?
: Told you so, Tsukasa. You should listen to me more often.
: Stop making so many silly decisions and I will.
Somehow, I wound up getting roped into agreeing to be a babysitter for both Chinami and Tsukasa soon.
That doesn’t sound exhausting at all.
Thankfully, I’ll at least have Touka there with me. And while that probably won’t really help either, it will definitely help me feel a little more normal as there’s at least someone who isn’t...
Well, someone who isn’t a full blown child there.
Plus, an environment like that sounds like the perfect place to fuck with her. And that is quickly becoming one of my favorite past times.
Anyway, the day comes to an end- and I find myself retreating back to my office.
